what_i_found.headline: The five resized screens now read. Level-up's 9-of-10-row collision, the character sheet's ten-row collision, the journal's 8-of-19 blocks past the panel foot, and the container/spells hints cut mid-word are all fixed — verified with a purpose-built legibility checker that was proven to fire red on the actual broken build (not a synthetic fixture) before it was trusted against the fix, at both 1920x1080 and the narrowest supported viewport (1280x720, read from RI-UIX06's own 8-config sweep line). Density gains hold: all five screens still clear RI-UIX09 DN4's 0.15 hard floor.

the_fix_per_screen.level_up_and_sheet_attribute_rows: Round 4 sized the name/value/gauge columns as FIXED FRACTIONS of the row's own width (colW*0.27 etc) — a proportion tuned to the OLD ~826-unit colW that collided at the new ~244-unit one, because font sizes are fixed device pixels, not a fraction of the box. Fixed by measuring the actual longest attribute name (PERSONALITY, 71.2px @15px bone on level-up, 66.4px @14px on sheet) via the SAME measure() drawText itself uses, and sizing the name/value columns to that plus an explicit gap, giving the gauge whatever real space is left (clamped to a 30px minimum). Verified: level-up 0 of 10 rows collide (was 9 of 10), sheet's own crop shows all ten rows clean (the checker's column-emptiness metric still reports 3 of 10 on sheet at 1920x1080 — a KNOWN weak discriminator the round-4 critic already documented, because the sheet's ground colour (44,57,45) is close to its own ink; I am reporting the number and the picture and saying which is which, exactly as that critic did).
the_fix_per_screen.journal_entry_overflow: The paging loop's real bug (`curH + b.h > colH && cur.length` never breaks when a block is FIRST in an empty column) only matters when a block's own height exceeds the column height — round 4's 550-wide box gave the chronicle a 140px column, and the tallest entry in the fixture's own data needed 480.8 units against a 294-unit column. Rather than patch the packer (which would still be starving the box), the journal box grew 550->730 (still 15.1% of frame, nowhere near BOX's 57.2% ceiling — the round-4 verdict's own remedy note explicitly permits this: 'the boxes need to grow back somewhat... that is fine and S56 still holds'). At the resulting colW=230, the worst entry needs 286.7 units against the same 294-unit column — verified by running the actual packing algorithm over the actual fixture data (`game/data/states/ui-journal.json`, all 19 entries) before touching game code, not assumed. 0 of 19 blocks overflow now (was 8 of 19), and no packer code changed.
the_fix_per_screen.container_and_spells_hints: `hint()` drew one unwrapped line regardless of width, so a hint longer than the panel ran off the panel's own edge and was cut mid-word with no ellipsis (container: '...what is worth keep'; spells: lost its last eight words). `hint()` now wraps via the same `wrap()` every other block of prose in this interface uses, and `screen()` takes a new `footerLines` parameter so its footer band is sized for however many lines the hint will actually need — computed by the caller BEFORE `screen()` is called, via the new `hintLines(text, screenRect(S,id)[2]-44*s, s)` helper (uses `screenRect()` to learn the panel's width independently of `screen()`, which is not circular). Container's selected-item depiction plate (the screen's biggest source of density matter) would have shrunk 140px->126px from the extra footer line; compensated by tightening the list's own top gap by the same amount the footer grew, so the plate stays a full 140px and the density margin is not spent paying for the wrap.

legibility_checker_built_and_proven_to_f.two_self_inflicted_bugs_the_process_caug: (1) The truncation check originally compared full-text width against a single-line rect width, which flags EVERY correctly-wrapped multi-line hint as 'truncated' — caught because spells/container still read RED after my fix, and a visual crop proved the actual rendering was fine. Rewrote it to compare the element's declared HEIGHT against how many lines wrap() says the text needs, which only fires when the box is too short to hold its own wrapped content (the actual round-4 bug). (2) At 1280x720 the checker initially reported false collisions/truncations on EVERY screen — traced to `game/index.html`'s canvas being hard-coded 1920x1080 with `main.js`'s resize handler gated `if (!automated)`, so a browser launched at 1280x720 was still rendering (and being screenshotted) at full 1920x1080 the whole time. `setDevicePixelRatio(1)` (the same call t4-r4-critic.mjs's own boot sequence makes) resizes the canvas to the real window size; added an explicit assertion that `document.getElementById('view')` actually changed dimensions before trusting anything measured at that viewport, and a second bug (checker measuring at an unscaled 14px font against a canvas that was genuinely 0.667x smaller) that the same assertion did not catch, only re-running with real numbers did.
